verdict.rationale: Crossplane's resources (Providers, Compositions, Configurations) are all defined as declarative Kubernetes YAML manifests, and community comments note this YAML is 'easy enough to commit to source control', implying data/config is inherently stored in an open, portable format rather than a proprietary export. However, there is no explicit documentation of an export command, data-migration tooling, or guarantee that all runtime state (not just config) can be extracted to leave the platform. missing for 10: explicit export/extraction feature or docs, confirmation that live resource state (not just desired-state YAML) is portable, and any migration guide for leaving Crossplane.
